newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia services deficit not seen improving.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia services deficit not seen improving.

text.p: Malaysia does not expect a major improvement in its services account deficit this year, though the trade gap has improved sharply in the first seven months, Bank Negara Deputy Governor Fong Weng Phak said on Thursday.
"I don't think the services account can improve that dramatically in a year," he told reporters at a conference on human resources in the financial services industry.

"You can't suddenly build ships over one year. You can't suddenly have education," he said referring to the country's heavy dependence on foreign ships for its trade and overseas institutions for education.
He said there was an impressive decline in the country's trade deficit in the first seven months of the year to 1.4 billion ringgit, from 6.9 billion in the same period of 1995.

"There is quite an improvement in the trade account", but the services account was unlikely to follow suit immediately, Fong said. "But, the (overall) current account would improve," he said, but did not give details.
